why: Who a VERIFIED bridge caller acts as, and what it is FOR. The key is the email of the OIDC token main.verify_caller accepted. `for` is one of three. `probe`: admitted to the service for /probe and refused on /op; it acts as nobody. `fleet-agent`: acts as `principal` on /op and may not state an author. `chair`: the conference chair; it must state an author and a request on every op, and `personas` lists the only authors it may name. A caller must ALSO be on the service's BRIDGE_CALLERS allowlist and hold run.invoker on the service: three independent gates, and this is the one that decides whose name goes in gov:audit.
how_to_change: Change one line, in a reviewed PR, AFTER the service account exists and the owner has approved it (docs/REDIS-PRIMARY.md, D2). tests/test_redis_tool_bridge.py holds each line to LEAST PRIVILEGE: a probe account acts as nobody; a fleet agent's principal must be able to write fleet: and conf:; the chair's must be able to read and write conf:persona: and NOTHING else. It also refuses a deploy allowlist that names a caller with no line here.
pilot: THE PILOT (conference docs/PERSONA-WRITE-CONFIRMATION-A1.md, section 12): the chair is the ONLY /op caller, for get and set of conf:persona:<day>:<persona> for the personas listed. Aya's runtime account keeps what it had before /op existed: the probe. THE BRIDGE TRUSTS THE CHAIR'S IDENTITY AND DOES NOT ENFORCE THE OWNER'S CONFIRMATION; that is checked in the chair alone. Putting a fleet agent on /op, or another persona on the chair's list, is its own reviewed decision. THE CANVAS (the owner, directly, 2026-10-20): the chair may also hset its own slot conf:canvas:<room>:chair, one text or diagram item of at most 512 bytes with no link, at most 20 posts an hour (op.py, canvas_refusal).
